analysis.title: Global Data Watch
key_insights: JPM says inflation persistence and a US labor market rebound point to the end of Fed 'magical thinking'. Its outlook rests on resilient global growth (tech spending plus a cyclical rebound in non-tech demand) and sticky core inflation.
Global core inflation ex China and Türkiye ran 3.4%ar in the three months through October. US core inflation is 3.2% PCE and 3.7% CPI on a 3-month annualized basis.

The Fed is expected to hike in December, with a median voter anticipating multiple hikes next year. A broad round of DM hikes is anticipated in December, but a Fed versus other central bank divergence could emerge next year as energy prices fall and other DM labor markets stay loose.
A recent Fed Board study finds higher DM inflation persistence and energy pass-through this decade. JPM's forecast downplays the pass-through but allows for longer tails.
Euro area: the 3Q26 employment stall is a reminder of weak spots. Growth is tracking above 1%, the ECB is still on track for at least two more hikes, and gas prices are sticky.
UK GDP grew 3%ar in 3Q. JPM raised its 4Q GDP forecast to 1.5% from 1.0%. A February BoE hike is the base case and December is a close call ahead of next week's CPI.
BoJ: the October summary of opinions signals continued hikes toward neutral at about a quarterly pace through mid 2027. The BoJ policy rate is 1.25%.

China: October exports +35.2%oya and imports +41.6%oya. Trade surplus fell to $105.3bn from $133.5bn. PPI +5.7%oya, CPI +0.7%oya. New loans contracted 100bn yuan, the first October contraction on record. The 5%ar GDP forecast depends on fiscal easing.

India: October CPI 6.1%oya, above the RBI's 6% upper tolerance limit. JPM raised its terminal repo rate forecast to 6.25% from 5.75%, with 25bp hikes in December, February and April and a risk of 50bp in December.

The 'productivity boom is less than meets the AI' essay argues US labor productivity growth (2.6%ar over 3 years) is mostly capital deepening (about 50%) and factor utilization (about 20%). True TFP is about a third of the gain (0.9%ar) and has stalled over the past year. This supports 'strong growth, sticky inflation, higher rates'.

Tariffs: JPM expects Section 301 and 232 tariffs soon to restore the effective rate to roughly the February pre-IEEPA level (about 14%, versus 11.2% today). Core inflation impact is about +0.1-0.2% over a year. Section 301 tariffs face legal challenges and the USCIT could rule by year-end.
APEC 2026 (Shenzhen, Nov 18-19): JPM expects selective cooperation and a possible US-China truce extension beyond 10 January 2027, not renewed integration or a regional trade agreement.
Euro area employment: core unemployment is 5.8% and periphery 7.3%. JPM expects employment growth of 0.3%ar in 4Q26 and 0.5%ar from 1Q27. Recovery depends on hiring in Germany and France.
Germany: JPM still sees about 2% of GDP fiscal easing over 2026-27 despite budget outturns running behind plan and a draft budgetary plan deficit of 4.6% of GDP in 2026 and 5.3% in 2027.

RBA: the cash rate is 4.85% after 125bp of hikes. The vote was 6-3 in November. JPM forecasts 50bp of easing in 2H27 and argues the RBA is inferring capacity from inflation, with a rising NAIRU assumption (4.75%).

US data: October CPI core +0.30%m/m, the third consecutive upside surprise, and core PPI +0.3%. Existing home sales fell 5.5% to 3.75mn saar, the lowest since August 2010. The 30-year mortgage rate was 7.33% in October.

Market pricing: December Fed hike priced at +27bp and June 2027 at +81bp. The 2Y yield rose 33bp on the week and about 88bp of cumulative hikes are priced by September 2027, versus about 47bp a week earlier.

Energy: Brent is about $96, off the $118 pre-midterm peak. JPM forecasts $80 in 4Q26 and $71 in 1Q27. JPM estimates a global oil surplus of 1.1 mbd in September and 1.4 mbd in October. European gas storage is 65.8% full versus 79% last year.

JPM Market Watch: stay bullish USD (long vs EUR, SEK, CAD), re-initiate long NOK vs EUR and SEK. In European credit, stay moderately positive for 2027 (OW 1-3Y IG, BBs over Bs, HY over leveraged loans). Forecast 2027 US HG gross issuance of $2.1tr.

sector_views.rationale: Moderately positive for 2027, favoring up-in-quality. Euro IG spread target 100bp (from 113bp) and HY 350bp (from 387bp), implying 7.0% and 8.25% total returns.

risk_factors: Inflation persistence and a more hawkish Fed than markets expected, with a possible 50bp December hike.
Energy and natural gas price rebounds, especially in Europe with low storage.
Soft euro area labor demand, especially in Germany and France.
Legal challenges to Section 301 tariffs and new tariff escalation.
A slowdown in US data-center and AI investment after the midterms, which would hit Taiwan, Korea and Chinese equipment exports in 2028 and beyond.
Housing weakness from mortgage rates above 7%.
El Niño food-price pressures in India, Mexico, Peru and South Africa.

vol_and_positioning: Energy open interest fell 14% WoW to $871bn, the lowest since August. Crude saw net outflows of $27bn.
Precious metals open interest rose 4% to $271bn with gold inflows of $2.9bn.
US curve bear flattened: the 2Y rose 33bp on the week.
geopolitical: US-Iran and energy developments, with Hormuz oil and LNG flows at about 50% of prewar levels.
Possible Trump-Xi meeting at APEC in Shenzhen (Nov 18-19) seeking a truce extension beyond 10 January 2027, and a possible Trump-Xi-Putin dialogue that is unconfirmed.
US midterm results (a 'blue wave') eroded the geopolitical oil risk premium and raised concerns over data-center investment.
Pending Section 301 'structural excess capacity' investigations into 16 economies and Section 232 actions.
Threatened 50% US tariffs on Canadian autos, trucks, parts and steel from January 1 absent a trade deal.
French presidential election: Le Pen leads polls and a Le Pen win is the base case.
South Africa local coalition negotiations in Gauteng metros ahead of a 26 November deadline.

tension_points.bull_case: The alternative narrative says the US labor productivity surge is an AI-driven structural shift, so the economy is already in the disinflationary supply stage and rates could fall. Some central bankers highlight this view.
tension_points.bear_case: JPM argues the boom is capital deepening and factor utilization, with TFP stalled. This keeps inflation sticky and supports higher rates, and jobless growth is not sustainable.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Sustained TFP gains like those of the late 1990s, or a slowdown in hyperscaler investment that fades the capital deepening contribution.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM's base case is a 25bp hike, supported by NY Fed President Williams seeing no signs of overheating and Vice Chair Bowman being comparatively dovish.
tension_points.bear_case: Governor Waller said a 50bp hike should be considered if core CPI was 0.3% or higher, and core CPI printed exactly 0.30%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Core CPI at or above 0.3% m/m triggered Waller's 50bp condition, so a hawkish FOMC discussion is likely.

theme_stances.key_argument: Inflation persistence and a labor market rebound point to the end of Fed 'magical thinking' and a policy pivot toward hikes.
theme_stances.evidence: close to the end of a long period of magical thinking

theme_stances.key_argument: The AI tech boom has yet to produce the sustained TFP gains of the late 1990s, so the productivity boom is less than meets the AI.
theme_stances.evidence: the AI tech boom has yet to generate the sustained TFP gains

theme_stances.key_argument: New Section 301 and 232 tariffs are likely to restore the effective rate to about 14%, with a modest inflation impact.
